proposal_text:
SUPERSEDES the proposal emitted at 2026-09-06T16:10:08Z (preserved as remediate-iter3.json). That proposal was not audited; it is withdrawn by its own author after an independent reviewer refuted three of its claims, all of which have since been confirmed by execution. The withdrawn proposal's own corrections to the entry-#749 design stand; what follows corrects the corrections. Entry #749's six grounds remain addressed, and the phase-keyed N=4 detector and the phase-reference regex tightening remain withdrawn. Nothing in qor/scripts/veto_pattern.py changes.

WHAT THE PREVIOUS DRAFT GOT WRONG, MEASURED.

First, it keyed on (session, target) and called session-scoping a virtue because it avoided a glob. Executed, that under-counts: phase 225's plan was audited once in session 2026-08-12T1705-fc410c and twice in 2026-08-17T1951-986e79, so its true depth on one scope is three and the session key sees a maximum of two. The reviewer's argument is accepted in full: this repository mandates session rotation before each plan, so a session boundary is procedure rather than evidence that a scope was set down and picked up fresh. Keying on the session measures session persistence, not scope difficulty, and it fails toward under-count, which is the wrong direction for a signal whose purpose is to fire before a cap.

Second, and worse, it offered "present in all 1741 records across 188 session histories" as evidence that the `target` field is reliable. Of those 1741 records, 1484 -- eighty-five percent -- are in a single synthetic fixture directory, .qor/gates/sess-12345/, which .gitignore line 23 excludes from the repository. The real corpus is 257 records across 187 session files. The reliability claim was therefore measured overwhelmingly against generated data, which is the same defect class this cluster has been vetoing since entry #743: a figure taken at the wrong unit and quoted as though taken at the right one. The corrected statement is that `target` is present in all 257 real records.

Third, its measured firing set of six depended on an undisclosed filter. The script that produced it dropped directories whose name begins with "sess-", and the proposal did not say so. Unfiltered, the fixture's 989 records against docs/plan-qor-phaseXX.md make that one scope the largest in the corpus, and at N=4 the set is eight rather than six. A proposal that quietly filters its own measurement is not measuring.

(a) THE KEY, CORRECTED. The normalised `target` field from .qor/gates/<session_id>/audit_history.jsonl, aggregated across sessions, NOT keyed by session. Normalisation replaces backslashes with forward slashes: seven records carry Windows separators and phases 217 and 218 are each split across both forms. The field is present in all 257 real records. Seven records from phases 101 through 107 carry a prose title such as "Phase 101: PyPI Publication Hardening P0 (GH #118 partial)" rather than a path; they remain distinct keys at count one and are harmless at any threshold, but the key is not guaranteed to be a path and nothing should assume it is.

FIXTURE EXCLUSION, WHICH THE KEY NOW REQUIRES. Aggregating across sessions means reading every session directory, so the synthetic corpus must be excluded by name rather than by an unstated convenience. .gitignore line 23 already names .qor/gates/sess-12345/, so the exclusion is not an invention; it must be implemented explicitly and pinned by a test, because nothing in audit_history's reader is gitignore-aware today. This also means the local and CI corpora differ: CI never sees the fixture, so any test that reads the live corpus must be CI-environment-honest and branch on the directory's absence rather than assuming it.

(b) THE HOOK POINT AND THE THRESHOLD, UNCHANGED AND NOW INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. A third mode of qor/scripts/cycle_count_escalator.py alongside `check` and `check_session_total`, returning an EscalationRecommendation with escalation_reason="scope-count", surfaced at /qor-audit Step 0.5 and /qor-plan Step 2c.

audit_history.append fires inside gate_chain.write_gate_artifact, after the verdict; Step 0.5 runs "before engaging adversarial mode". So at Step 0.5 of attempt N the history holds N-1 records, and a threshold N fires as attempt N+1 begins, leaving 4-N of the five attempts. N=3 fires entering attempt 4 and leaves two. N=4 would fire entering attempt 5 with zero in reserve, which is later than the cap is useful. This is the property entry #749 showed no placement of four can deliver.

MEASURED AT N=3 ON THE CORRECTED KEY, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Thirteen of 191 real scopes reach three or more: the phase 223 plan (5), 258 (5), 261 (5), 265 (5), the phase 223 remediation document (4), 248 (4), and 224, 225, 249, 250, 251, 253 and 254 at three each. Three were abandoned at the cap; ten recovered and sealed. Ten false positives against three true ones. The ratio is worse than the withdrawn draft reported, because phase 225 joins at three once the session key is dropped, and it is stated here rather than filtered.

(c) WHAT A FIRING COSTS. No new Process Shadow Genome event. The existing escalator returns a recommendation to the operator and emits nothing when it fires; the only genome cost is the existing severity-2 orchestration_override event on operator decline. That cost collapses to a single signature across all declines only if the reason string is fixed, because check_shadow_threshold._signature digests the whole details blob when no `gate`, `capability` or `pattern` key is present, and orchestration_override.record puts `reason` into details. /qor-plan already passes interpolated reasons such as f"user override: {result.errors}", which never collapse. This proposal requires the literal, uninterpolated reason "scope-count escalation declined". Ten false positives therefore cost ten operator declines and severity 2 in total, not severity 20.

DEPENDENCY, BLOCKING. That decline-once story is false today for the mode this resembles. cycle_count_escalator.check_session_total calls _suppression_active(session_id, None), and the helper returns False whenever first_match_ts is None, so the marker is never read and a declined cumulative escalation re-fires on every subsequent audit in the session. Its docstring claims the opposite. Filed as GH #447. Until it is fixed, ten false-positive scopes nag repeatedly and each decline appends another event, so this proposal is not implementable ahead of it. The scope mode must pass the timestamp of the oldest audit record contributing to the over-threshold scope.

(d) CLOSURE ENFORCER: tests/test_cycle_count_escalator.py. It gains: the scope mode fires at three and not at two, from synthetic records; `docs\plan.md` and `docs/plan.md` count as one scope; records from an excluded fixture directory do not contribute, built from the sess-12345 shape; a scope split across two sessions counts as one, built from the phase 225 shape, which is the defect that withdrew the previous draft; a decline recorded after the oldest contributing record suppresses the next check while one recorded before it does not, which is GH #447 and fails today; and a live-corpus binding that asserts an INVARIANT and not a set -- every reported scope has a normalised count of at least three and every scope at three or more is reported -- skipping cleanly when the local-only fixture directory is absent, as it is in CI. The exact-firing-set form entry #749 ruled inadmissible under doctrine-test-discipline.md line 35 is not used. The unbounded "does not alter any other result for any input" test is dropped; in its place, `check` and `check_session_total` return identical values before and after, on the fixture corpus those two already own.

(e) RESIDUAL LIMITS, NAMED. The key is a path string, so a plan renamed mid-cycle reads as two scopes and under-counts; no instance of that exists in the corpus, and it is not defended against. The prose-title records from phases 101 through 107 are keys that are not paths. And the corpus that any live binding reads differs between a developer machine and CI by 1484 records, which is why the binding asserts an invariant and skips rather than counting.

DOCTRINE HALF, unchanged by every verdict in this cluster and standing on entries #743 through #747: a characterization corpus offered as a behaviour-preserving refactor's safety argument must be derived from the code's acceptance conditions rather than enumerated by the author.

PROCESS FINDING. Entry #749 recorded that the tribunal seeded the defect it vetoed. This draft records the symmetric one: the author, having been vetoed twice for unexecuted claims, wrote a third proposal whose central evidence figure was 85 percent synthetic and whose firing set depended on a filter it did not disclose. Four artifacts into this remediation and the recurring failure has never been the reasoning; it has been the unit the numbers were taken at. The countermeasure that follows from four instances is narrow and mechanical: a proposal may not quote a corpus figure without stating what was excluded from it and why.
supersedes: the unaudited proposal preserved as remediate-iter3.json; the audited chain runs through META_LEDGER entry #749
